title: Powers of elements of a finite purely inseparable algebra lie in the base after localization
statement: Let $A'$ be a Noetherian integral domain with fraction field $K'$, and let $E$ be a finite $A'$-algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] that is a domain with fraction field $L$. Assume that $L/K'$ is finite purely inseparable [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. There is a nonzero $s\in A'$ such that, writing $A''=A'[1/s]$ and $E''=E\otimes_{A'}A''$, the following hold: if $K'$ has characteristic $0$, then $E''=A''$; if $K'$ has characteristic $p>0$, then for every $x\in E''$ there is an $n\ge 0$ with $x^{p^n}$ in the image of $A''$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0BR5 (algebra-lemma-purely-inseparable), power calculation for a finite purely inseparable extension and localization

proof.text: Choose a finite set g spanning E as an A'-module using Module.Finite.fg_top [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The finite purely inseparable field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] has a uniform exponent N by Mathlib IsPurelyInseparable.hasExponent_of_finiteDimensional. For each e in g, write the q^N-th power of its image in L as the image of c in K', with q=ringExpChar K'. IsLocalization.surj writes c times a nonzero denominator t as a numerator b in A'. The scalar tower equalities and injectivity E -> L give (algebraMap A' E t)*e^(q^N)=algebraMap A' E b in E. Let s be the product of these denominators. It is nonzero; each t divides s, so its image is a unit in Localization.Away s. Map the equality to E tensor Localization.Away s and multiply by the inverse of that unit. This is the fully proved private helper localized_generator_powers.

source.place: Section 0BR5, denominator-clearing input to Lemma 0BR8; implemented using Mathlib.FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Exponent and the fraction-ring and tensor-product APIs

proof.text: The fully proved private helper powers_from_generators propagates a fixed positive power k that distributes over addition. First use Submodule.span_induction to extend the generator condition to all e in E: addition uses the distributing identity, and scalar multiplication uses the k-th power of the scalar in the base. Then use TensorProduct.induction_on: pure tensors are the product of e tensor 1 and includeRight(b); sums use the same distributing identity. All base witnesses are explicit sums or products, so no embedding of the tensor product in L is required.

source.place: Section 0BR5, denominator-clearing input to Lemma 0BR8; implemented using Mathlib.FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Exponent and the fraction-ring and tensor-product APIs

proof.text: In characteristic zero, ringExpChar K'=1, hence q^N=1. Apply powers_from_generators with k=1, whose additive identity is tautological, to obtain surjectivity of includeRight. This proves the characteristic-zero clause for the same s.

source.place: Section 0BR5, denominator-clearing input to Lemma 0BR8; implemented using Mathlib.FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Exponent and the fraction-ring and tensor-product APIs

proof.text: In characteristic p>0, Fact p.Prime and CharP K' p imply ExpChar K' p, so ringExpChar K'=p. If the tensor product is subsingleton the required witness is n=0 and a=0. Otherwise transfer CharP from K' to A' using the injective fraction-field map, then to the nontrivial tensor product using CharP.of_ringHom_of_ne_zero. Mathlib add_pow_char_pow supplies distributivity of the power p^N. Apply powers_from_generators with k=p^N, which is nonzero, and choose n=N. This proves the characteristic-p clause for the same s.
